title: 60% of Canada's Electricity Comes From Water #shorts
summary: More than half of Canada's electricity, about 60%, is generated from hydroelectricity (Canada Energy Regulator, 2021). The US got about 6% from hydro in 2025 (EIA).
sources: More than half of the electricity in Canada (60%) is generated from hydroelectricity; 625.7 TWh produced in 2021 (Canada Energy Regulator, Canada Energy Profile): https://cer-rec.gc.ca/en/data-analysis/energy-markets/provincial-territorial-energy-profiles/provincial-territorial-energy-profiles-canada.html

US utility-scale generation in 2025: renewables about 24%; natural gas about 41%, nuclear about 18%, coal about 17%, wind about 11%, solar about 7%, hydropower about 6% (EIA, Electricity explained: electricity in the US): https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/electricity/electricity-in-the-us.php

Supply must match demand for the grid to stay stable; transformers step voltage up and down between the power plant, long-distance lines and distribution lines; the Eastern and Western interconnections are linked to Canada's grid (EIA, Electricity explained: delivery to consumers): https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/electricity/delivery-to-consumers.php

scenes.narration: About {60%|sixty percent} of Canada's electricity comes from water.
Hydroelectric dams. Falling water spins the generators.
In the US last year? About {6%|six percent} came from hydro.
And the US grids in the East and West connect to Canada's.
So in Canada, the lights mostly run on rivers. About {60%|sixty percent}.
